title: Types and connection of instruments
summary: How to connect and use the main electrical test instruments (voltmeter, ohmmeter, ammeter, wattmeter) and the ranges of the low resistance, insulation resistance and earth fault loop impedance testers.

sections.heading: Quantities and instruments
paragraphs: There are four main quantities we measure when testing electrical installations. Each has its own type of instrument. In practice, instruments are often multifunctional and can measure a number of these quantities, if not all of them.
bullets: Voltage is measured with a voltmeter
Current is measured with an ammeter
Resistance is measured with an ohmmeter
Power is measured with a wattmeter

sections.heading: Measuring voltage and resistance
paragraphs: To measure voltage between two points, set the voltmeter to the correct range and connect it between those two points. For example, to measure the voltage across resistor R2, connect the voltmeter across R2.

To measure the resistance of a cable or component, set the ohmmeter to the correct range and connect it between the ends of the cable or across the component. The supply voltage must be isolated before measuring resistance.
bullets: Isolate the supply before measuring resistance of cables or components
It is better to remove components or disconnect cables, to avoid incorrect readings caused by parallel resistance paths

sections.heading: Measuring current
paragraphs: To measure current, set the ammeter to the correct range, break the circuit and connect the ammeter between the two points. Measuring the current flowing through the entire circuit means the ammeter sits in the circuit itself.
bullets: Ammeter: break the circuit and connect it between the two points

sections.heading: Measuring power
paragraphs: Power = Voltage × Current. A wattmeter is therefore a combined voltage and current meter. It measures both quantities and produces a readout that is the product of the two.
bullets: A common wattmeter is the home electricity meter, calibrated to read power consumption in kilowatt/hours

sections.heading: Low resistance ohmmeter
paragraphs: This instrument is used to test the continuity of protective conductors, the continuity of ring final conductors and polarity.

sections.heading: Insulation resistance tester
paragraphs: This instrument is used to test the insulation resistance of cables and the electrical separation of circuits.
bullets: Applied test voltages: 250 V, 500 V, 1000 V

sections.heading: Earth fault loop impedance tester
paragraphs: This instrument is used to test earth fault loop impedance and prospective fault current.
bullets: Range: 20 Ω (for TN and some TT earthing systems)
Range: 200 Ω and 2000 Ω (for TT earthing systems)

flashcards.front: Which instrument measures voltage, current, resistance and power?
flashcards.back: Voltage: voltmeter. Current: ammeter. Resistance: ohmmeter. Power: wattmeter.

flashcards.front: How do you connect a voltmeter to measure the voltage across a resistor?
flashcards.back: Set the correct range and connect the voltmeter between the two points, that is, across the resistor.

flashcards.front: How do you connect an ohmmeter to measure a component?
flashcards.back: Set the correct range and connect it across the component, or between the ends of the cable.

flashcards.front: What must be done to the supply before measuring resistance?
flashcards.back: The supply voltage must be isolated.

flashcards.front: Why is it better to remove components or disconnect cables when measuring resistance?
flashcards.back: To remove the chance of incorrect readings caused by parallel resistance paths.

flashcards.front: How is an ammeter connected to measure circuit current?
flashcards.back: Set the correct range, break the circuit and connect the ammeter between the two points.
The product of voltage and current (Power = Voltage x Current), because it is a combined voltage and ammeter.

flashcards.front: Give a common example of a wattmeter.
flashcards.back: The electricity meter in a home, calibrated to read power consumption in kilowatt/hours.

flashcards.front: What is a low resistance ohmmeter used to test?
flashcards.back: Continuity of protective conductors, continuity of ring final conductors, and polarity.

flashcards.front: What range should a low resistance ohmmeter cover?
What test voltages does an insulation resistance tester apply?
What does an earth fault loop impedance tester test?
flashcards.back: Earth fault loop impedance and prospective fault current.

quiz.q: Which instrument should be used to measure the continuity of a ring final conductor?
quiz.why: A low resistance ohmmeter tests continuity of protective and ring final conductors, and polarity.

quiz.q: How is an ammeter connected to measure the current in a whole circuit?
options: Break the circuit and connect it between the two points
Connect it across the supply terminals
Connect it in parallel across a resistor
Connect it across the ends of the cable with the supply on
quiz.why: The circuit must be broken so the ammeter is connected between the two points.

quiz.q: What must be done before measuring the resistance of a cable?
options: Set the instrument to measure power
Connect the meter in series with the load
quiz.why: The supply voltage must be isolated before measuring resistance of cables or components.

quiz.q: Which set of test voltages is applied by an insulation resistance tester?
quiz.why: Insulation resistance testers apply 250 V, 500 V and 1000 V.

quiz.q: Why is it better to disconnect components when measuring resistance?
options: To avoid readings affected by parallel resistance paths
To allow the wattmeter to read power
quiz.why: Removing components removes the chance of incorrect readings caused by parallel resistance paths.

quiz.q: A wattmeter gives a readout that is the product of which two quantities?
quiz.why: Power = Voltage x Current, so a wattmeter combines voltage and current measurements.

quiz.q: Which range is stated for an earth fault loop impedance tester on TT earthing systems?
quiz.why: 200 Ω and 2000 Ω ranges are for TT earthing systems.

quiz.q: Which instrument tests the electrical separation of circuits?
quiz.why: Insulation resistance testers test cable insulation and electrical separation of circuits.

quiz.q: Which quantities does an earth fault loop impedance tester test?
options: Earth fault loop impedance and prospective fault current
quiz.why: It tests earth fault loop impedance and prospective fault current.
